reason: The local change holds: .cell (&9C2A) is entered only by fall-through, and LDA col_ptr+1 (never 0: from straight_sprite_hi after BNE known, then only INCed) ; ADC #&FF leaves C = 1, so dropping the SEC at &9C2B saves 2 cycles and 1 byte. But the 1-byte slide is not cost-neutral, and the candidate does not count it. Everything after &9C2B in bank 4 moves down 1, including sprite_straight.6502's sprite data straight_35..straight_4a (&A530-&B3xx, about 14 page boundaries). draw_column reads that data in its hottest loop, LDA (d_ptr),Y at .byte and .part_byte, plus LDA (col_ptr),Y. Moving the data down 1 is the same as moving each page boundary P up 1 relative to it. For a full cell whose d_ptr lies in (P-7, P), the cell saves 1 cycle. A cell whose d_ptr was exactly P (no crossing before) now has base P-1, so its reads at Y = 1..7 all cross: +7 cycles. Which case a column hits depends on the line, which is set by the mover's y. Ground soldiers and level-flying craft keep a fixed y, so some sprites will pay +7 per boundary column on every draw. That can outweigh the 2-cycle x 9.4-a-pass saving, and is data-dependent and unmeasured. straight_sprite_hi (&A4E4,X) also changes: X = &1C stops crossing (-1). The pixel and mask tables (&0400-&04FF, main RAM) do not move. The self-modified operands mask_operand/pix_operand(_2) are written through their labels, so the move does not break them. draw_column's own branches stay within page &9C. The net cycle change can't be established without measuring, so refuted. The byte-neutral alternative avoids all of this.
